publisher: Eau de Paris (regie publique de la Ville de Paris)
title: Catalogue des tarifs et redevances 2026 — annexe à la délibération
archive_note: Assembled by the collector from the fetched document, not dumped byte for byte: the sections that price a residential water account are transcribed in full and the eleven pages of laboratory analyses, works, branch connections, domain occupation and merchandise are omitted, none of which reaches a household bill. Every line of sections 1 and 3 that can fall on one is present, because the value of the capture is the enumeration. A byte-exact capture of the PDF would be the stronger archive and is worth taking when the site can be reached from a machine that stores files.
establishes: The decomposition the record was waiting for. The catalogue prices every line of a Paris water bill separately, HT and TTC, with the VAT rate against each — which is what makes this a decomposition rather than an allocation.

The drinking-water lines, all at 5.50% VAT: supply of drinking water 1,1319 HT / 1,1942 TTC per m3; low-flow support levy (EPTB) 0,0070 / 0,0074; abstraction levy on water resources 0,0880 / 0,0928; Voies Navigables de France 0,0160 / 0,0169; municipal share (Ville de Paris) 0,0150 / 0,0158; drinking-water network performance levy 0,0385 / 0,0406; drinking-water consumption levy (Agence de l'eau) 0,3400 / 0,3587.
The wastewater lines, all at 10.00% VAT: collection (SAP) 0,6090 / 0,6699; transport and treatment (SIAAP) 1,5440 / 1,6984; collective sanitation performance levy 0,1230 / 0,1353.
The subscription schedule the published headline excludes: 6,21 HT / 6,55 TTC per quarter at 15 mm, rising by diameter to 826,39 / 871,84 at 500 mm, all at 5.50% VAT.

That nothing else recurs on a metered household. The rest of section 3 prices one-off events — individualisation of a collective meter, event and provisional access, penalties, bench tests, closure and reopening, payment rejections — and section 2 prices the separate non-potable network, which is not a household supply.
does_not_establish: A designated residential meter diameter. Fourteen are priced and none is named as the ordinary household connection. 15 mm is the smallest and is used here as the smallest priced connection, which is a reading and not a designation.

How a household in a collectively metered building is billed. The catalogue prices the individualisation of a collective meter as a service, which implies the collective meter is the common case in Paris; what a resident of such a building pays is a different question and is not answered here.
The wastewater rates as Eau de Paris's own. Three of the ten volumetric lines are collected on behalf of third parties whose assemblies set them, which the catalogue states on its face.
reconciliations_passed: Every one of the ten volumetric lines reconciles HT to TTC at its own stated VAT rate, to the fourth decimal, with no exception: 1,1319 x 1.055 = 1,19415 printed as 1,1942; 0,3400 x 1.055 = 0,3587 exactly; 1,5440 x 1.10 = 1,6984 exactly.

The ten TTC lines sum to 4,2300 per m3. Eau de Paris publishes the total price of a cubic metre at 1 January 2026 as 4,23 EUR TTC hors abonnement. Exact — and it is what turns a headline into a decomposition.
The drinking-water side sums to 1,7264 TTC and the wastewater side to 2,5036. 1,6364 x 1.055 = 1,726402 and 2,2760 x 1.10 = 2,5036, so each side also closes against its own VAT rate.
The subscription reconciles: 6,21 x 1.055 = 6,55155, printed as 6,55 per quarter.
